title: External adapter UTF-8 boundary split corrupts structured tool responses
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Multiple customers reported tool/function-calling failures where structured JSON returned by external adapters is rejected by the runtime parser. Failures correlate with responses containing multi-byte UTF-8 characters (emoji, non-latin glyphs). The runtime's streaming reassembly logic can split multi-byte characters across internal chunk boundaries, producing invalid UTF-8 sequences and JSON.parse errors in downstream structured output handling.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a tool adapter that returns a JSON body containing emoji and long string fields (e.g., { "response": "Status: ✅ – processing complete" }).
2) Send a request through a gateway that uses chunked transfer encoding or the dedicated proxy path (seen on Dedicated and Private deployments).
3) Observe the streaming path reassembly in the runtime (continuous batching / prefix streaming enabled).
4) Reproduce by forcing small chunk sizes so multi-byte code points are split across emitted chunks.
5) Runtime attempts to parse structured tool output as it arrives and raises a parse error when decoding encounters truncated UTF-8 sequences.
observed_behavior: Runtime logs show JSON parse errors (UnicodeDecodeError / invalid UTF-8) and tool invocation fails. Affected customer applications see function/tool-calling fail with 500-level errors or truncated responses. Issue appears in Hosted (rare), Dedicated (frequent on older proxies), and Private (on-prem proxies with chunked transfer tunings).
expected_behavior: Streaming reassembly should be UTF-8 safe: the runtime should buffer incomplete multi-byte sequences across chunk boundaries, decode only complete sequences, and present valid JSON to the structured output parser so tool/function calls succeed regardless of emoji or language in responses.
customer_reports: ACME Corp (support-5823): intermittent tool failures when returning i18n status messages with emoji; started after Dedicated proxy upgrade.
FinLedger (support-5890): reranking adapter responses rejected with parse errors during peak traffic; observed only on on-prem proxy path.
PilotHealth (support-5938): streaming response for long patient notes with Unicode characters occasionally corrupts downstream function call payload.
impact_summary: High: multiple paying customers experiencing production failures in tool-calling flows. Impacts Hosted for a subset of edge cases, but widespread in Dedicated and Private when proxies introduce small chunk sizes or middleboxes re-chunk traffic. Can cause data loss in critical function outputs and increases error rates above SLOs.
mitigation: 1) Temporary gateway rule to base64-encode adapter response bodies for affected customers (applied per-tenant).
root_cause_summary: Reassembly code treats streaming chunks as UTF-8 strings and slices by buffer length rather than ensuring rune/codepoint completeness. When a multi-byte UTF-8 character is split across two chunks, the first chunk contains an incomplete sequence which is immediately decoded/parsed, producing an error. Additionally, some proxies re-chunk responses which increases likelihood of splits.
proposed_solution:
1) Replace current byte-slicing reassembly with a UTF-8-aware streaming decode using a TextDecoder-like incremental API (or equivalent Rust/Go decoder) that preserves incomplete sequences until the next chunk arrives.
2) Centralize reassembly logic into a single well-tested library used by hosted, dedicated proxy, and private agent code paths.
3) Add unit tests covering multi-byte boundary splits (emoji, 3- and 4-byte sequences) and fuzz tests for random chunk boundaries.
4) Add e2e tests using a re-chunking proxy simulator.
5) Patch runtime and proxy packages; ship as runtime-1.21 patch and proxy-0.46.1.
rollback_plan: If the fix causes regressions, rollback by switching affected customers back to the temporary base64 gateway transform (fast toggle) while we iterate. Rolling back runtime version on Dedicated customers via canary groups if necessary.
testing_plan: Unit tests for UTF-8 boundary cases (emoji, multi-byte CJK) in reassembly library.
Integration tests: simulate chunked transfer with controlled split points and verify structured parser accepts concatenated output.
E2E: run full toolcall flow against a staging gateway that re-chunks payloads; validate with sample adapters from customers.
Load test: ensure reassembly change does not materially affect latency under high concurrency or memory pressure.
rollout: Canary rollout: hosted canary (5% traffic) and two Dedicated customers (non-critical) for 24h -> 25% for 48h -> 100% plus Private customers via agent upgrade. Communicate maintenance window for private/on-prem agent upgrades.
